text: We had a very positive experience at Chiang Mai Hospital following a motorbike accident. From arrival to discharge, the service was efficient and professional, with virtually no waiting time and a consistently kind and attentive staff. Several team members spoke excellent English, and when someone did not, they immediately used a translator to ensure clear communication. The medical care was thorough and reassuring, and the staff were very accommodating to our needs throughout our visit. We were also pleasantly surprised to be informed that a government motorbike accident insurance scheme covered our medical costs, which was handled smoothly and transparently. We are grateful for the high standard of care and would confidently recommend this hospital.

Seen in minutes, nurses were kind and helpful, the doctor spoke superb English and had a great bedside manner. Given treatment and back out in an hour. £66 for the consultation and a whole raft of meds. 100% recommend this hospital from my experience today

text: As a foreigner living in Thailand, I was honestly a bit nervous about seeing a doctor. I was worried there might be a language barrier and that I wouldn’t be able to fully explain or understand everything. But to my surprise (and relief!), they provide translators for many languages.The translator I met—AJ—was amazing! He was incredibly professional and could clearly convey everything the doctor said (I could catch some parts myself, so I knew he was spot on). At first, I actually thought he was from my own country because he spoke the language so fluently and naturally. 😄 Turns out he’s Thai! Thank you, AJ, for patiently answering all my questions and making the whole experience smooth and stress-free!

text: Excellent. The staff, nurses, and doctors are very kind and take great care of patients. They address all the elderly patients as "parents" and are never rude or dismissive when asked for directions. They are truly kind. Those with a universal healthcare card can use it; various health checkups are available. Check your eligibility!

Overall, everything was okay. The communication and information provided were good, which is great considering I've had much worse experiences elsewhere. Maybe I was just lucky this time, haha. But overall, everything was fine. I switched to using my universal healthcare benefits here.

I went to the hospital on Saturday evening. The doctors and nurses were very attentive, but the staff in the X-ray room made an unacceptable statement. I took my 5-year-old child for an X-ray, and they wouldn't let the parent go in. I understand that, but their words to the child – "Mom can't go in, don't cry, you won't get the picture" – were very harsh. The 5-year-old was crying and scared, even though he wasn't struggling or crying loudly. He's had X-rays many times before, and other hospitals allow adults to go in. I was very unimpressed with the male staff member, around 30 years old, who told the child to hold his breath while crying and afraid of the X-ray. I wondered if that would affect the child's health and the treatment results. Please reprimand this staff member.

I received treatment at this hospital on May 6th, 2026. The doctor provided excellent care and communication; there were no problems with the treatment itself. However, I would like to criticize the behavior of the nurse/staff at the …

Honestly, the service isn't much different from a government hospital, just fewer people and faster. The equipment isn't as advanced either. I went for both ear and dental checkups, and it was like nothing was found. I have tinnitus, but my hearing is normal, so the doctor didn't order any further tests, even though I expected them to help find the cause or do some additional tests. But there was nothing. When I went for dental work, the doctor who performed the procedure for patients using the 30-baht card was quite elderly. She was a bit grumpy when it came to orthodontics, just like other reviews mentioned. I just told her that I had braces before and now I have a cavity that was hurting, so I wanted to get it checked. She grumbled something like, "You should go to the orthodontist who did your braces, not me." But I had already finished my orthodontics, and the problem just started, so I came to see a doctor for a checkup. If it could be filled, I wouldn't have to spend money at a clinic. I tried to stay calm and asked if I could get the cavity filled if an X-ray showed more decay. That's when she sent me to the X-ray room downstairs, but the 30-baht card doesn't cover that; I had to pay myself. The only good thing is that the staff are lovely. But the doctor might still be inexperienced. Anyone considering transferring their 30-baht healthcare benefits here should give it a try. However, personally, I think it's better to switch back to a public hospital. There might be longer wait times, but they have complete equipment, and you won't have to go through the hassle of being referred elsewhere, as this hospital doesn't have all the necessary departments.
The public relations department knows absolutely nothing.
